lines: Iron bars, sunk deep into the rock. Beyond them the dark goes on toward the Warden's hall.
Under Nib's floor, through the old grate, a cold draught hums. Like something very large, very far down, waiting to be struck.

steps.text: Drop through the grate in Nib's floor: hold ↓ and jump.

lines: It is very dark here.
Even the dark seems to have been lost.
A bell, hung in the dark. Bigger than a house. Green with age.
It used to ring at dusk, so that lost things would know it was time to come home.
The bell hangs still. It has said what it had to say.
You take the rope in your teeth and pull with your whole weight.
The note goes on for a long time. Up through the rock. Into the walls. Into you.
Far above, iron grinds against stone. Something that was shut is open.
...Was that a bell? Nightpaw, I heard a bell.
The moth says it's nothing. She says not to turn round.

else.text: The bars in the Long Dark have lifted. Climb the Old Sluice.

lines: Little graves, in rows. A domino, a matchbox, half a spoon, each pushed upright into the dirt.
Somebody buried every lost thing that ended here, for as long as they could.
HERE LIES A LEFT MITTEN
It waited for a hand.
HERE LIES A SMALL BRASS KEY
It never found out what it opened.
HERE LIES THE GRAVEKEEPER
The rest of the stone is blank. There was nobody left to finish it.
The top of the well. An old bucket. A rope gone soft with rot. A grate, rusted into the stone.
Through the bars: rain, and a strip of night sky.
Somewhere up there is a window with the curtains still open, and a bed with nobody in it.
MIRA
Scratched into the stone with something small and sharp. A hairpin, maybe.
Under it, much older, in a hand you don't know: and ELSIE, and TOM, and a name too worn to read.
A grey whetstone, worn hollow in the middle by somebody's patient knife.

steps.title: Whetstone
steps.text: Your claws are sharper. Every scratch bites deeper.

lines: Everything the Warden ever caught. He couldn't bear to put any of it down.
Keys. Shoes. A pram wheel. A small collar with a bell on it, and nothing inside the collar.
Tally marks. Thousands of them, scratched in neat rows, one for every thing he caught.
The last row stops halfway.

steps.title: 4TH WICKMOOR SCOUTS
steps.text: A label from a tent peg. Somewhere a tent leaned a little to the left for the rest of its life, and nobody ever knew why.

steps.title: THE GOOD SCISSORS
steps.text: Kept in the second drawer. Lost in a move. Everyone in the house blamed everyone else, quietly, for thirty years.

steps.title: IF FOUND RETURN TO ADA, 12 FENN ROW
steps.text: A luggage label. The handwriting gets shakier toward the end of the address, as if the writer already knew.

steps.title: MR. BUTTONS
steps.text: Stitched inside a bear's ear. He went up to the attic 'just for now'. Now lasted a very long time.

steps.title: BISCUIT
steps.text: A dog's collar tag, bitten at the edge. He waited by the gate every evening. One evening he went looking instead.

steps.title: PIP
steps.text: A tag too small for any collar. Whoever Pip was, they sang. The cage door was left open, just the once.

steps.title: HENRY'S
steps.text: Written on the sole of a tin soldier's boot in careful pen. Henry grew up. The soldier did not.

steps.title: GRANDAD'S CHAIR. DO NOT SIT.
steps.text: Nobody sat in it for years. Then it was carried out to the kerb, still empty, in the rain.

lines: The nursery door. Locked from this side.
On the other side, very faintly, a music box is playing, and somebody is humming along to it, out of tune.

steps.text: The keyhole is shaped like a little lamb. Somebody must have kept the key.

lines: The old upstairs hall, flooded to the knee.
Portraits of the family line the walls. Somebody has rubbed all of their faces away, very carefully, with a thumb.
A child in a sailor collar, holding a nightlight shaped like a moth.
The face has been rubbed out like the others. The moth has not.
A small room off the hall. A rocking chair, a basket of knitting, a cold cup of tea.
The chair is rocking. Nobody is in it.
NANNY BRIGGS, 1911
Stern, kind, very tired. She held the children on her lap and sang them the rhyme, the way every nanny in Wickmoor did.
Lose a penny, lose a key...
A little iron key with a lamb for its bow, hung on a hook by somebody who meant to come back for it.

steps.title: The Lamb Key
steps.text: It opens the nursery door at the far end of the Bathtub.

lines: Behind you, the chair stops rocking.
...hush now, hush, and hold on tight...
Nightpaw? There's an old lady in the dark up here. She's singing my song. She says she used to sing it to a girl who had a moth for a nightlight.

steps.text: Back to the Bathtub's far door. Climb the Drain.

lines: Everything that was put away "just for now", under sheets, in the dust.
Some of the sheets are breathing.
A tall mirror, its silver gone to grey.
In it: the attic, the sheets, the dust, the little rocking horse.
No cat.
Another whetstone, hidden behind the chimney where nobody would find it. Somebody wanted something kept sharp up here.

steps.title: Whetstone
steps.text: Your claws are sharper still.

steps.title: BABY'S FIRST
steps.text: A ribbon that once held a lock of hair, folded in tissue. The hair is gone. The ribbon has kept its shape.

steps.title: DOLLY (THE NICE ONE)
steps.text: There must have been a not-nice one. Nobody remembers which one that was, or what it did.

steps.title: NANNY BRIGGS
steps.text: A brass badge, rubbed bright on one side by a thumb. She was in this house for forty years. Nobody came for her things.

steps.title: ROSALIND, AGED 5
steps.text: Name tape from a nightgown, sewn in crooked by someone in a hurry who loved her anyway.

steps.title: LAMB
steps.text: From a nightlight shaped like a lamb. It was switched off one night, and nobody ever switched it back on.

steps.title: M.
steps.text: Just a letter, scratched into the base of a tin soldier. It could have been anyone's. It could have been the child who loved a moth.
